items.titel: Beslisnota bij Kamerbrief over voortgang evaluatie Rijkshuisvestingsstelsel 2020-2025 en toezegging identiteitskaart BES

document.tekst_begin: Aanleiding In de tweede helft van 2025 is de vijfjaarlijkse evaluatie van het Rijkshuisvestingsstelsel (hierna: RHS) uitgevoerd. Het doel van de evaluatie is om de doelmatigheid en doeltreffendheid van twee deelstelsels (rijkskantoren en specialties) in kaart te brengen. Daarbij zijn aanbevelingen tot verbetering gedaan. Op 13 maart 2026 heeft u de rapporten van de evaluatie RHS aangeboden aan de Kamer1. Op 10 juli 2026 heeft u een inhoudelijke beleidsreactie verzonden aan de Kamer2, waarin is toegezegd om in oktober de Kamer nader te informeren over de voortgang van de ingezette acties. Geadviseerd besluit U wordt geadviseerd: - Akkoord te geven op verzending van de Kamerbrief, met het oog op het Commissiedebat Slagvaardige Overheid en regeldruk op 28 oktober 2026, conform de gedane toezegging (beleidsreactie 10 juli jl.) de TK vóór het debat een voortgangsbrief te sturen. Kern De evaluatie Rijkshuisvestingsstelsel 2020-2025 laat zien dat het rijkskantorenstelsel effectiever en doelmatiger is geworden. items.titel: Canalised Urban Waterways, Palimpsest Landscapes and Climate Adaptation: Comparison of Ecomorphological Trajectories from Isparta and Chelmsford
items.samenvatting_bron: This paper examines canalised urban waterways as active ecomorphological agents in the Anthropocene city through a comparative study of Isparta, Türkiye, and Chelmsford, United Kingdom. Focusing on Isparta’s Çayboyu canal and associated stream system, and Chelmsford’s canalised corridor shaped by the Rivers Chelmer and Can, the paper investigates how urban waterways form and modify relationships between urban morphology, spatial memory and public space. Canalised streams and rivers are reviewed as palimpsest landscapes and spatial corridors that continue to influence urban form, multispecies movement, and everyday experience in the age of climate change and redevelopment pressures. This study reviews how each waterway has been altered, marginalised, and reactivated within the evolving processes of urban development. The findings demonstrate that the integration of town centres depends not only on standard design solutions or location, but also on the ability to make ecological and everyday spatial relations visible and accessible. In this sense, ecomorphological trajectories contribute to debates in river restoration, ecological and morphological approaches and multispecies urban studies. Finally, the paper suggests that more permeable and adaptive approaches to canalised waterways could support spatial scenarios for reconnecting town centres with blue-green infrastructure under climate uncertainty.

items.titel: Mammalian–Environmental–DNA-Derived Probabilistic Modeling Reveals Re-Established Trophic and Co-Habitation Network Structure in Fire-Affected Terrestrial Communities
items.samenvatting_bron: Climate change threatens natural ecosystems with more frequent and intense extreme weather events, including forest fires. This study evaluated mammalian communities, a primary bio-indicator of forest health, in Uljin Forest, using both traditional camera traps and advanced environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding. Fire severity at the study sites was categorized based on field observations and satellite images using the differenced Normalized Burn Ratio. Water basins were installed for 7 days, after which the water was collected for eDNA extraction. A multi-primer approach using mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit 1 and 12S rRNA genes was employed. Comparative analysis of the mammalian relative abundance indicated that while camera traps remain the optimal tool for monitoring large mammals, eDNA methods were significantly more effective for quantifying small, cryptic species. Although long-term effects remain observable in the biodiversity and abundance of mammalian communities, Bayesian network analysis at the order level inferred positive ecological signals three years post-fire, with the food-web-related and cohabitation dynamics re-established. eDNA metabarcoding improved mammal detection relative to traditional methods and enabled probabilistic modelling to reveal ecological structure that would not be possible solely with biodiversity analysis. Overall, this multi-primer/multi-analysis approach highlights the potential of eDNA for ecosystem health monitoring.

items.titel: A washable glue for trapping pests on sticky boards in honey bee colonies
items.samenvatting_bron: Varroa mites are major pests of honey bee colonies and contribute to colony losses. Entomopathogenic fungi are a promising tool for Varroa control, but evaluating their efficacy requires follow-up infection assays. Conventional sticky board adhesives, such as petroleum jelly or vegetable oil, can trap fallen mites but are difficult to remove before testing. We developed a water-soluble glue made from cooked corn starch and glycerin that can be easily washed away with water or ethanol. The glue is prepared by cooking starch in water until thickened and then mixing it with glycerin to achieve the desired consistency. This adhesive simplifies mite recovery from sticky boards, reducing labor during mite collection and facilitating infection assays. It may also have applications in water-soluble insect traps and environmental DNA detection.

items.titel: Mapping groundwater-dependent vegetation in temperate climates on the example of Central Germany
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Groundwater-dependent ecosystems are biodiversity hotspots that provide habitat for specialized species. The European Union (EU) Water Framework Directive (WFD) stresses the importance of identifying and protecting these ecosystems. So far, most studies focus on (semi-) arid regions, where groundwater use by ecosystems is both more prevalent and easier to detect. In this study, we adapt groundwater-dependent vegetation (GDV) mapping approaches developed for dry climates to temperate regions by replacing seasonal drought-based indicators with contrasts between dry and wet years. We implement this concept by integrating for the first time to our knowledge, ECOSTRESS evapotranspiration data with high-resolution remote sensing, regional geospatial data and botanical field observations. To test our framework, we trained and validated random forest models with eight predictor variables using 166 vegetation plots to identify GDV in Central Germany. Ground-truth GDV plots prefer cooler, wetter, nutrient-richer and more acidic to alkaline environments compared to non-GDV. items.titel: Communicating Coastal Resilience
items.samenvatting_bron: Coastal resilience increasingly relies on ecosystem-based adaptation, nature-based solutions, hybrid infrastructure, seawalls, flood management, erosion control, and spatial planning. Yet infrastructure is also a communicative and political process through which risk, trust, participation, and responsibility are negotiated. Synthesising 30 recent peer-reviewed studies, this review examines communication, community participation, governance, equity, and infrastructure assessment. It finds that communication is often treated as supplementary, participation remains vulnerable to tokenism, and nature-based or hybrid systems require long-term governance, maintenance, and justice-sensitive evaluation. Coastal communities are also differentiated by place attachment, livelihoods, vulnerability, and trust. The paper proposes a communicative governance model in which resilient infrastructure is socially interpreted, co-produced, institutionally accountable, and equitably maintained.

items.titel: Effects of Climate Change and Adaptation Strategies for Coastal Infrastructure
items.samenvatting_bron: Coastal regions across the world are among the most productive and densely inhabited zones on Earth, yet they stand at the front line of an accelerating climate emergency. Sea level rise, intensifying storm surges, chronic flooding, saltwater intrusion, coastal erosion, and extreme heat events are reshaping the physical and socioeconomic landscape of these zones at a pace that overwhelms traditional planning and engineering responses. This chapter examines the multidimensional effects of climate change on coastal infrastructure and explores the spectrum of adaptation strategies available to planners, engineers, policymakers, and communities. Drawing on a synthesis of peer-reviewed research, case studies from vulnerable coastal regions in Asia, Africa, the Americas, and the Pacific Islands, and emerging frameworks in climate-resilient design, the chapter evaluates hard engineering defenses, nature-based solutions, hybrid approaches, and governance innovations.

items.titel: Regulating Climate-Resilient Coastal Infrastructure
items.samenvatting_bron: Coastal infrastructure is now a legal concern as ports, roads, homes, wetlands, and services face seas, storms, erosion, and flooding. Many systems rely on fragmented, short-term, grey-led rules. This chapter develops a framework for climate-resilient coastal infrastructure. It argues that law should combine climate-risk duties, smart technologies, nature-based solutions, adaptive governance, and justice. Using doctrinal and policy methods, it reviews planning, environmental, disaster-risk, and infrastructure regulation. It finds that coastal law must recognize ecosystems as infrastructure, regulate risk data, require participation, and prevent maladaptation. The implication is fair, anticipatory, and accountable governance.
